newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer battered to 8-month loss by sports.
newsitem.headline: Amer battered to 8-month loss by sports.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer, dogged by weak sales in golf, tennis and ski equipment, said on Thursday it had fallen deeply into the red in January-August and would stay clearly loss-making this year.

Amer, whose Wilson tennis racquets are used by top professionals including Pete Sampras and Steffi Graf, swung to a January-August loss of 206 million markka ($45.1 million) from a 36 million markka profit before extraordinary items a year earlier.
In a statement, Amer repeated a warning that it will remain "clearly loss-making" this year. Last year it booked a 142 million markka profit before extras and tax.
Amer said its net sales, which fell 24 percent to 3.22 billion markka from 4.23 billion a year ago, would continue to shrink.

The loss was largely in line with market expectations but Amer, whose stock had climbed on speculative demand ahead of the report, fell after the news to trade down 4.00 markka or about four percent at 102.00 in late Helsinki trade.
Amer said it expected losses from all three of its big-brand sports units, Wilson, MacGregor and Atomic, which together made up 76 percent of January-August net sales.
Problems at Wilson were mainly due to continued difficulties in golf club and ball sales, as well as lower sales and profitability in clothing and baseball products, Amer said.
But Amer said Wilson would remain in all its current product areas. "Wilson is maintaining its strong market position in all team sports product categories in the U.S.," Amer said.
While MacGregor Golf Company sales had been above target in the Asia-Pacific region, Amer said they fell short of expectations in the U.S. and Europe.
It forecast only a slight increase in MacGregor net sales for the unit this year, and said losses are likely to remain at the 1995 level, which was 32 million markka.

"Measures relating to the company's unprofitable operations are still being examined, and a final decision should have been made by the year end," said Amer, which has promised to restructure the unit.
Amer said its Atomic unit, also headed for full-year losses, had suffered occasional delivery troubles throughout the year. It said the market for alpine ski equipment was still declining.
But its said demand for snowboards would rise fast and it expected snowboard sales to double in 1996 from an unspecified 1995 level. ($ = 4.567 Finnish Markka)
